notes:
Summary: QuickLynx builds a low-latency market data summarization and decision-assist chat used by traders and risk ops. High concurrencies during market open (spikes x5). Cost-sensitive — running 24/7 inference; CPU/GPU unit economics matter. Interested in Redwood to replace an in-house Triton + bespoke batching stack.

Key requirements / asks:
- Primary workloads: short-turn chat (avg 12 tokens), embeddings for similarity search on new trades, reranking for fast trade signals.
- Latency targets: p95 end-to-end <= 120ms for short responses, p99 tail < 300ms during steady state; burst handling at market-open with <500ms graceful degradation.
- Throughput targets: sustained 200 req/s, burst to 1k req/s for 3-5 minute windows.
- Cost sensitivity: seeking 30–40% lower $/token vs current infra.
- Model preferences: open-family equivalence to Llama2-Chat / Falcon variants; willing to try quantized variants (int8 / 4-bit) if quality delta acceptable.
- Routing/fallback: require automated fallback to smaller quantized model when Dedicated capacity saturated; prefer policy-level routing by latency SLA.
- Caching needs: prefix/KV caching for repeated query patterns (instrument tickers), multi-tenant split caches, TTL controls.
- Batching: dynamic batching with strict latency ceilings — need recommendations and profiling for optimal batch size distribution across traffic regimes.

Security & compliance notes:
- Must support SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, and detailed audit logs for model inputs/outputs.
- Data residency: US-only; legal has stricter controls for PII in trade annotations.
- Completed base security questionnaire; asked for SOC2 attestation copy and architecture diagram for private deployment.

Perf benchmarking request (customer asks):
- Redwood to run a two-day benchmark in staging using QuickLynx prompt mix (mix file in Drive). Objective: measure p50/p95/p99 token-level latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M-tokens for these configs: (A) hosted API baseline, (B) Dedicated GPU pool with dynamic batching + prefix cache, (C) Dedicated with int8 quantization, (D) Private on-prem with 4-bit quantization. Include tail-latency graphs, batch-size distribution, and kernel-level breakdown (kernel selection/triton vs cuBLAS/TensorRT where applicable).
- Customer expects actionable tuning: recommended batch sizes per payload length, cache TTLs, and quantization profile with quality deltas on a 200-sample eval set.
